en: The Haraṃba Stotra composed by Gaurī.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Gaurī said:
O Elephant-faced One, who brings about the play of knowledge, do you not recognize me, the supreme Avasarpiṇī?
O Gaṇeśa, protect me; otherwise, endowed with devotion to you, I shall immediately cast off this body. || 1 ||
O Vighneśa, Heramba, Mahodara, beloved Lambodara, Acyuta who increases my love;
O destroyer of obstacles and destroyer of hosts of demons, protect me, who am endowed with devotion unto You, from the Daityas. || 2 ||
Are you deluded by the expansion of worldly success and intellect? Or are you sleeping at night?
Are you occupied with deliberations for the sake of gaining a hundred thousand [coins]? Or have you forgotten me and remained comfortably settled? (3)
O God of gods, have you been well-restrained by attachment to food and various offerings?
O Vakratuṇḍa, have you been taken up by the leader of the Gaṇas for the sake of sweetmeats and various diversions? 4.
O Great-Souled One, you have abandoned the enjoyment of your own bliss and forgotten even your handmaid;
yet you are eager for infinite pastimes—is it because you are situated in a great crisis for the sake of protecting your devotees? || 5 ||
Aha! You have been remembered by the gods, who are skilled in drinking the nectar of Gaṇeśa, as well as by the lords of the asuras;
therefore, you are now occupied with various rites for their sake, having abandoned me, your servant, who am devoted to no other. || 6 ||
Protect me, who am most wretched, O Supreme Lord, for You are established everywhere within all hearts.
O Lord, You are the Deliverer without delay; O Brahmā, O Īśa, O God, salutations, salutations unto You!
O Great-souled One, if the name "one who prides himself on devotion" is not primarily found in the Veda,
then come, O Lord of Gods, slay the son of Aditi, and protect me, your maidservant whose feet are fixed in your heart.
"Alas! Nothing is far from you at all; O Lord of Intellect, why have you not come?
O God who is well-reflected upon, I shall abandon this body and thus achieve fame that is the opposite [of my current state]. || 9 ||
Protect me, protect me, O ocean of compassion! Forgive my offenses;
moment by moment, I am your servant and must be protected especially.
Even as Pārvatī was thus praising him, Śaṅkara, endowed with awakening consciousness, became aware of it upon hearing the cry of "Alas! Alas! from the leaders of the Gaṇas, O Creator.
Having mentally remembered Gaṇeśa, he arrived mounted upon his bull;
in an instant, seeing that king of the Daityas, he struck him with a hand-drum (ḍamaru).
Then, seeing Śiva, he also rushed forward to embrace him;
indeed, Śiva’s weapons, such as the trident and others, became blunted.
Seeing that supreme marvel, Maheśvara was struck with fear; O Prajāpati, he remembered the Lord of the Gaṇas, who also [appeared] for the sake of removing obstacles.
Having heard the hymn of Pārvatī, Gajānana arrived.
Thus ends the Heramba-stotra as spoken in the Mudgala Purāṇa.
